content: We need number of carbonyl groups in the sample's molecule. We have no direct description of molecule. We can use IR spectra to detect C=O stretch. Or carbon NMR maybe shows carbonyl carbons ~190-220 ppm. Use IR tool to get spectrum, then count carbonyl peaks. Probably easier: IR will show strong absorption around 1700 cm-1 for each carbonyl. But overlapping may be ambiguous. Could also use carbon NMR to see carbonyl signals. Use carbon_nmr_spectra tool to get 13C NMR. Then count peaks in carbonyl region (190-220 ppm). Let's do carbon NMR first.
